open_obligations: Map the safety-case agent, debate game and honesty premises to the exact formal protocol.
Check whether the protocol theorem addresses deployment continuity and tolerated errors.

The protocol result concerns debate protocols in which the honest strategy can always succeed using a simulation of a polynomial number of steps against a dishonest strategy allowed exponentially many simulation steps, for stochastic AI systems, and the protocol abstract names no training procedure; the safety-case agent is trained via debate, subject to exploration guarantees, with honesty maintained through online training in deployment. Check whether that agent and its debate game meet the protocol's assumptions.
out.rationale: The safety-case abstract names debate performance and honesty premises; the protocol abstract offers a different formal debate result.
out.scope: candidate correspondence between the safety-case sketch's claim (2), that good performance in the debate game implies that the system is mostly honest, and the protocol abstract's result that the honest strategy can always succeed using a simulation of a polynomial number of steps, for stochastic AI systems, even when the dishonest strategy is allowed to use exponentially many simulation steps

open_obligations: The safety case's AI R&D agent is trained via debate, subject to exploration guarantees, with honesty maintained throughout deployment via online training, and claim (2) concerns that system's honesty; the empirical study (Khan et al.) optimises expert debaters for persuasiveness in an unsupervised manner and reports the answer accuracy of non-expert models and humans who lack the information the experts have in an analogous setting, rather than judging a superhuman system. Compare these judges, populations, tasks, outcomes and training procedures.
Do not treat answer accuracy as a deployment safety certificate.
out.rationale: The empirical abstract studies weaker judges selecting answers; the safety-case sketch concerns a different agent and harm argument.
out.scope: candidate correspondence between the empirical finding that optimising expert debaters for persuasiveness in an unsupervised manner improves non-expert ability to identify the truth in debates and the proposed deployment safety case's claim (2), that good performance in the debate game implies that the system is mostly honest
